correctness.rationale: Multiplicativity gives Δ=σ(n)−2n=H(p+q+1)−pq with H=2^{a+1}−1. Δ>0 yields p²−2Hp−H<0, hence p≤H+floor(sqrt(H(H+1))), namely 6,14,30. If p<H, Δ>2^a p forces q|Δ and thus q|H(p+1), so q≤H(p+1); if p>H, positivity forces (p−H)q<H(p+1); p=H yields an impossible extra factor 2 in Δ. These inequalities bound all p,q, so finite enumeration is exhaustive. Independent implementation enumerated every prime pair under the proved bounds before applying divisibility (7,66,382 pairs for a=1,2,3) and found exactly the five displayed pairs; each σ and omitted divisor checked by direct integer arithmetic. The finite checker has proved bounds, not an arbitrary cutoff.
